significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish a form-(iii) predictive temporal law—successful jailbreaks show an "elevated-then-decaying" refusal trajectory, genuine refusals a rising trajectory, and benign responses a low trajectory—plus a form-(ii) causal mechanism in which intervention at the "collapse point" prevents harmful continuation. This fixes expectations across future tokens and attack classes, and would show whether the static refusal-direction account used by Arditi et al., "Refusal in Language Models Is Mediated by a Single Direction" (NeurIPS 2024), is dynamically sufficient; it establishes both a behavioral phenomenon and a mechanistic explanation rather than merely another decodable direction. The true and false states are distinguishable, and a broad negative result would rule out delayed commitment collapse as a common jailbreak mechanism, favoring immediate, static, or attack-specific pathways rather than merely reporting failure to find a feature. Topic substitution lowers the assessment materially: generic mechanistic LLM safety would not earn this score, whereas the quoted cross-token ordering and early-to-late predictive coupling are specific additions above the topic-median refusal-probe-and-steering hypothesis.

reach.justification: The named handles are the per-token "refusal commitment trajectory," an "early-warning monitor," a detected "collapse point," and a "minimal one-shot repair" that re-injects the refusal direction. The monitor is ex ante with respect to eventual jailbreak success and harmful continuation—using the "first k generated tokens" leaves an action window—although it may not precede every leaked output token. After per-model re-extraction, the asserted rising-versus-decaying trajectory relation still predicts what should be found across Llama, Qwen, and Gemma families and diverse jailbreak classes, so the transferable conclusion is more than a procedure for rediscovering an unconstrained direction; auditors or serving-system operators could use it to gate or interrupt generation. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: safety interpretability alone supplies no such temporal predictor or intervention trigger, while these specific handles support practitioner uptake beyond researchers analyzing refusal representations.
